Setting up the MacBook Neo (Nina) for College

A simple guide to getting Nina's MacBook ready for college.

Choose one of the topics below.

1. Initial Setup

  1. Turn on the MacBook and choose English (UK) and the United Kingdom as the region.
  2. Connect to your home Wi-Fi.
  3. Create Nina's Mac login account with a strong password she will remember.
  4. Set up Touch ID so she can unlock the Mac and approve purchases securely.
  5. Turn on Location Services so Find My Mac and Maps can work properly.
  6. Allow macOS to install any available software updates before setting up college apps.
  7. Set the correct date, time zone and keyboard layout.

It is worth keeping the first setup simple. Most settings can be changed later in System Settings.

2. Apple ID & iCloud

  1. Sign in with Nina's own Apple Account. Do not use somebody else's account.
  2. Turn on Find My Mac. This is important if the MacBook is ever lost or stolen.
  3. Enable iCloud Drive for documents she wants available across Apple devices.
  4. Enable Passwords & Keychain so saved passwords can be securely synchronised.
  5. Decide whether Photos, Messages and Desktop/Documents should sync to iCloud.

If storage is limited, there is no need to put every college file into iCloud. Google Drive may be the better place for college work because Salisbury 6th Form College uses Google Workspace.

3. Apps & Software

For Biology, Psychology and Physical Education, the MacBook should cover the normal work required: documents, presentations, spreadsheets, PDFs, research and online learning.

Microsoft 365:

  1. Open Safari and go to m365.cloud.microsoft/apps.
  2. Sign in with Nina's Salisbury 6th Form College email address and password.
  3. If Install apps is available, choose Microsoft 365 apps and download the installer.
  4. Open the downloaded .pkg file and follow the installation steps.
  5. Open Word or Excel and sign in again with the college account to activate the licence.

If there is no Install apps option, the college account may only provide web access. S6C currently emphasises Google Workspace, so Word, Excel and PowerPoint may not be essential for day-to-day college work.

Useful additional apps include Google Chrome, Adobe Acrobat Reader if required, and Zoom or Microsoft Teams if teachers use them.

4. College Systems

Salisbury 6th Form College provides students with Google Workspace. Nina should use her college account for school email and online learning resources.

  1. Sign into Gmail, Google Drive, Google Docs, Sheets and Slides using the college account.
  2. Bookmark the main college login pages in Safari or Chrome.
  3. When at college, connect to the college Wi-Fi using the instructions provided by S6C.
  4. Keep personal and college Google accounts separate so files are saved to the correct place.

S6C gives a general warning that Apple laptops are not fully compatible with every piece of college software. However, Biology, Psychology and PE are not among the subjects S6C identifies as having specialist computer requirements.

5. Files & Organisation

A simple structure will make coursework much easier to find.

Create a main folder called College, then subfolders such as:

  • Biology
  • Psychology
  • Physical Education

Inside each subject folder, use folders for topics, coursework, revision and past papers.

Use clear filenames such as Biology - Cell Structure - Notes rather than names such as Document 1.

For work that must be submitted through college systems, keep the master copy in Google Drive where possible. Avoid leaving important work only in the Downloads folder.

6. Security & Privacy

  1. Use a strong Mac login password and enable Touch ID.
  2. Make sure Find My Mac is enabled.
  3. Leave FileVault encryption enabled if offered during setup.
  4. Install macOS security updates when prompted.
  5. Do not install software from unfamiliar websites.
  6. Be cautious with messages asking for passwords, verification codes or payment details.
  7. Keep college and Apple account recovery details up to date.

macOS includes strong built-in security, so third-party antivirus software is not normally necessary for ordinary college use if the Mac is kept updated and software is installed from reputable sources.

7. Battery & Power

  1. Leave Optimised Battery Charging enabled.
  2. There is no need to run the battery completely flat before charging.
  3. Charging overnight is fine; the Mac manages the charging process automatically.
  4. Reduce screen brightness when away from a charger if longer battery life is needed.
  5. Close applications that are not being used if battery life is becoming low.

For college, it is still sensible to start the day with a well-charged battery and carry the charger when practical.

8. Study Tools

The MacBook includes several useful tools without installing anything extra:

  • Preview for opening, annotating and signing PDFs.
  • Screenshot tools using Shift-Command-3 or Shift-Command-4.
  • Notes for quick revision notes and checklists.
  • Spotlight for quickly finding files, apps and information.
  • Focus modes to reduce notifications while studying.

For Biology and Psychology, Google Docs is useful for written notes and assignments, while Google Sheets or Excel can be used for data and simple statistical work. For PE, presentation software can be useful for practical analysis and coursework.

9. Troubleshooting

If an app freezes: press Option-Command-Escape, select the app and choose Force Quit.

If the Mac behaves oddly: restart it before trying anything more complicated.

If Wi-Fi will not connect: turn Wi-Fi off and on, forget and rejoin the network, or restart the Mac.

If storage is running low: go to System Settings → General → Storage to see what is using space.

If Nina forgets a password: use the official Apple or college account recovery process rather than creating a second account.

If the Mac is lost: use Find My from another Apple device or via iCloud as soon as possible.

If a college website or application does not work correctly on the Mac, check with S6C before changing major settings or buying software.
